hasPart.name: Reading a routing table
hasPart.text: For ordinary destination-based forwarding, compare the destination with installed prefixes. Of the matching routes, the one with the longest prefix wins. For example, 192.0.2.17 matches both 192.0.2.0/24 and 192.0.2.0/25 and follows the /25 entry. Follow the next hop listed for that entry.

hasPart.name: Diagnosing default route problems
hasPart.text: The IPv4 prefix 0.0.0.0/0 matches every destination. More specific matches take precedence. With no matching route, a router cannot forward the packet. A wrong default next hop can affect previously unmatched destinations even while directly connected and specifically routed networks remain reachable.
